Article 3
The regulation regarding the Empowerment and Protection of Women and Children aims to:
a. guarantee the fulfillment of the rights of every woman and child to survival, growth and development;
b. improve the quality of life of women, children and the quality of families; c. increase the institutional capacity for women's empowerment and child protection in the regions, including the development of gender and child data systems; and
d. provide protection of women's rights and fulfillment of children's rights including special protection for children from various forms of violence and other discriminatory treatment.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Sarolangun Regency.
2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regent is the Regent of Sarolangun.
5. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is a regional people's representative institution that is positioned as an element of Regional Government administration.
6. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities.
7. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
8. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women.
9. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of social and cultural conditions of society.
10. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.
11. Gender mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of national development program policies.
12. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
13. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
14. Guardian is a person or body who in reality exercises parental authority over a child.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree.
16. Community is individuals, families, communities, religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, business world and corporations, community organizations, social organizations, women's and gender study centers, mass media or other similar entities.
17. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence, exploitation, discrimination, and neglect.
18. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic substances, and other addictive substances (napza) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of maltreatment and neglect.
19. Safe house is a shelter or temporary protection house for victims during the assistance process to ensure the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators and is only known to interested parties for reasons of victim safety and security.
20. Child-friendly regency is a regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitment and resources of government, community, business world, and media that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights and special protection of children.

Part Five
Right to Education, Utilization of Leisure Time and Cultural Activities Article 24 Every Child has the right to obtain the right to education, utilization of leisure time and cultural activities, as referred to in Article 14 letter d, in the form of:
a. participating in early childhood education;
b. obtaining the widest possible opportunity to obtain education; c. the right to develop talents, interests and creative abilities; d. recreation; and
e. having leisure time to rest and engage in various artistic, cultural and sports activities.

Article 12
(1) Empowerment of women in the field of law as referred to in Article 8 letter d includes:
a. increasing awareness and knowledge in the field of law through communication, information and education services; and
b. facilitation of access and legal consultation services.
(2) Empowerment of women in the field of law as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

4.4.rationale: Pasal 26 (and Pasal 24) concern children’s right to education and government provision of education services (wajib belajar 12 tahun, inclusive education, scholarships, child-friendly schools). This is not 'prevention through education' in the sense of violence-prevention education content (e.g., teaching non-violence, consent, gender equality, anti-VAW curricula). The judge treated general education access/quality measures as violence-prevention education, which is too broad. The Indonesian text does not clearly state prevention of VAW through educational curricula; thus the golden 'No' is consistent and the error is the judge’s overly lenient mapping.

5.5.evaluator_rationale: The policy explicitly mentions coordinating participation of other institutions including international assistance for women’s empowerment and child protection.

Article 29
Regional Government shall endeavor to fulfill the Right to Special Protection for children by:
a. formulating programs to prevent children from being involved in situations and conditions as referred to in Article 27 paragraph (3);
b. providing access to public services and social security for children with disabilities; and
c. providing 24 (twenty-four) hour complaint service facilities, Shelters, rehabilitation centers and orphanages.

Article 12

5.5.rationale: The Indonesian Pasal 33 ayat (1) huruf f says "mengkoordinasikan peran serta dunia usaha dan kelembagaan lain, termasuk bantuan internasional". This mentions international assistance as a possible supporting input, but it does not explicitly describe engagement/partnership with international organizations (named IOs/UN agencies/NGOs) as stakeholders, nor a mechanism for their participation beyond a general clause. The indicator is specifically 'International organisations engagement'; the judge equated 'international assistance' with active engagement of international organizations. Given the text’s vagueness, the golden 'No' is plausible and the judge’s 'Yes' is an over-interpretation.

6.2.evaluator_rationale: None of the provided passages explicitly mention women victims of human trafficking or specify protection measures targeted to trafficked women (references to trafficking appear only in relation to children, not women).

Article 13
(1) Protection of women includes:
a. social protection;
b. economic protection; and
c. legal protection.
(2) Social protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is to ensure the survival of women in the form of social protection in order to ensure the fulfillment of proper living needs.
(3) Economic protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is to prevent and address the risk of vulnerability resulting from shocks and social vulnerability of a person, family, group and/or community for the survival of women.
(4) Legal protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is implemented in terms of providing protection to women who become witnesses and victims of acts of violence and discrimination.

CHAPTER IV
SAFE HOUSE
Article 30
(1) Women and child victims of violence who require continuous handling have the right to stay in a safe house.
(2) The safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) provides a place or temporary safe shelter for victims of violence until their rights are restored.
(3) The organization and management of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by regional apparatus that performs functions in the field of women and child empowerment.
(4) Further provisions regarding the organization of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Protection of Women

Article 7
(1) Regional Governments have the obligation and responsibility for the empowerment and protection of women.
(2) The efforts for empowerment and protection of women as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. determination of policies, programs, and activities for improving the quality of life of women related to the fields of development, education, health, economy, law, Human Rights and politics, environment and socio-culture;
b. provision of services to women especially to victims of violence, female workers, elderly women, and women with disabilities, victims of conflict and victims affected by disasters; and
c. implementation of gender mainstreaming in government institutions, women's study centers, research and development institutions, non-governmental institutions.
(3) The efforts for empowerment and protection of women as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with the prevailing laws and regulations.
(4) The empowerment and protection of women shall be coordinated by the Regional Apparatus that administers regional government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

6.2.rationale: The judge is correct that trafficking is explicitly mentioned for children (Pasal 27 ayat (3) huruf i: "anak korban penculikan, penjualan, dan/atau perdagangan"), but the indicator here is 'Trafficking victims' under an intersectional approach (implying women/VaW policy attention to trafficked women). In the Indonesian provisions on women, there is no explicit mention of "perdagangan orang"/trafficking victims as a targeted group for women’s protection services; Pasal 7(2)(b) lists service targets (victims of violence, female workers, elderly women, women with disabilities, conflict/disaster victims) but not trafficking victims. Therefore the golden 'Yes' appears incorrect for this indicator as framed; the policy addresses trafficking victims only in the child-protection section.

7.3.evaluator_rationale: The policy explicitly mentions coordinating participation of institutions including international assistance for women's empowerment and child protection, indicating international support/donor involvement.

Article 37
(1) Financing for the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection is sourced from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget. 7.3.rationale: Funding sources are governed by Pasal 37: financing comes from APBD and may come from "sumber pembiayaan lain yang sah dan tidak mengikat" (other legitimate and non-binding sources). This does not explicitly mention international donors. Pasal 33’s "termasuk bantuan internasional" is about coordinating participation/assistance in guidance activities, not a budget line or funding source commitment. The judge conflated 'international assistance' with 'international donors as funding sources'. Given the Indonesian text, the golden 'No' is consistent and the judge’s 'Yes' is an overreach.
